author: Fable review
title: Diagnosis: the model learns to recognize messages, not to parse them
body:
Source: the independent Fable review, `eval/reports/current/data-improvement-plan-fable.md` (status PROPOSAL, 2026-09-29; produced read-only on the CPU from existing corpora, suites and prediction files). The plan recommends; the owner decides.

The training corpus is a deterministic function of a small closed inventory: **648 question-frame ids, 201 constructions, 135 relation phrases, 250 target skeletons and 6,515 role values**. Given a message's masked template, the target skeleton has **0.001 bits** of entropy (1,805 of 1,809 templates with ≥2 rows map to exactly one skeleton). A 135M model fits that inventory (dev 92–98%): sealed-test accuracy is **96%** when the frame and every name were seen in training and **67%** when neither was. Out of distribution the inventory is absent (97% of the wild suite's gold relation phrases and 94% of its role values never occur in training), so the model recalls the nearest known phrase and generates the nearest known name ("wrong relation", "corrupted name").

Three measurable causes: (1) closed vocabularies with high repetition (every relation phrase seen ~500 times, every value ~22 times); (2) Romanian targets require translation, not formalization; (3) a bimodal length distribution and a synthetic register.

author: Fable review
title: The test measures unseen frames; dev does not (tolerant execution by novelty slice)
body:
Source: the independent Fable review, `eval/reports/current/data-improvement-plan-fable.md` (status PROPOSAL, 2026-09-29; produced read-only on the CPU from existing corpora, suites and prediction files). The plan recommends; the owner decides. Section 1.1, 4,730 short test rows, Q8_0:

| Slice | n | SmolLM2-135M | Gemma 3 270M |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| frame seen / unseen | 1,063 / 3,576 | 91.2% / 75.3% | 87.5% / 76.3% |
| every construction seen / some unseen | 1,638 / 1,506 | 81.3% / 61.4% | 80.6% / 64.9% |
| every role value seen / some unseen | 2,361 / 2,369 | 87.2% / 70.5% | 91.2% / 66.6% |
| seen frame + seen names | 626 | 96.3% | 96.8% |
| new frame + new names | 1,869 | 67.3% | 64.7% |
| RO frame seen / unseen | 377 / 1,240 | 88.1% / 64.6% | 86.7% / 71.5% |
| EN frame seen / unseen | 498 / 1,841 | 94.4% / 83.2% | 89.4% / 80.0% |

77.1% of short test rows use a frame that never occurs in train/dev; a frame seen even 1–49 times is learned as well as one seen 200 times. Dev shares every frame with train, so "selection on dev is selection for memorization".

author: Fable review
title: Closed relation vocabulary and generated (not copied) names
body:
Source: the independent Fable review, `eval/reports/current/data-improvement-plan-fable.md` (status PROPOSAL, 2026-09-29; produced read-only on the CPU from existing corpora, suites and prediction files). The plan recommends; the owner decides. Sections 1.3–1.4.

- **Relations:** 135 distinct phrases in train; the wild suite's gold has 1,073, of which 3.2% (distinct) are seen in train; the OOD domain axis 0%. In 91.5% of English training rows every content word of the phrase is in the message, so copy-and-lemmatize is learnable, but with 135 phrases each seen hundreds of times recall is cheaper than copying. Wild English relation errors dominate (31 of 40 sampled wild failures).
- **Names:** 6,515 distinct train values, 22 uses per value; wild values seen in train: 5.6%. Of 1,546 name-like SmolLM2 predictions on wild, 76% are exact message spans, **14.5% near-miss corruptions** ("Rahm" for Raiffeisen, "Ireland" for "Irlanda") and 8% not in the message at all. SmolLM2 spends 2.6 tokens per name word (Târgu Mureș 8, S.C. Verde-Nord S.R.L. 14). Gemma memorizes names more (91% seen vs 67% unseen).
- **What is not the problem (§1.7):** syntax (parse 99.9%), harness limits, `unclear`/numeric/universal rows (98–100%), eval strictness for the small models (0/30 false negatives). Model size alone is not the fix; spellfix helps noisy synthetic rows but not real text.

author: Fable review
title: Ranked ideas: open vocabularies first, then Romanian, length, honest dev, paraphrase and distillation
body:
Source: the independent Fable review, `eval/reports/current/data-improvement-plan-fable.md` (status PROPOSAL, 2026-09-29; produced read-only on the CPU from existing corpora, suites and prediction files). The plan recommends; the owner decides. Section 2, ranked by expected impact per unit of cost:

1. **Open name/value vocabulary with copy pressure** (≥30,000 distinct values, each used ≤3 times; exclude every wild/OOD name). Expected: unseen-name gap 17 → ≤6 points; wild name fidelity 76% → ≥90%. Low cost.
2. **Open relation vocabulary (English):** 10–30 constructions per predicate, then a large verb-frame resource with per-row predicates. Expected: construction gap 20 → ≤8; OOD construction/EN 55 → ≥70. Medium cost.
3. **Romanian target policy + parity** (D1): a large RO→EN dictionary through the data, or Romanian lemma targets linked by the host; ≥50% of Romanian rows without diacritics. Expected OOD RO 8 → 25–35 (a) or ≥45 (b).
4. **Mid-length realistic messages, capped long ones** (D4).
5. **Frame-disjoint dev split** and k-fold frame rotation: no accuracy gain, but honest selection (dev overstates the test by 14–19 points). Very low cost.
6. **Verified LLM paraphrase layer** (30–50% of rows, executable checks, independent meaning judge, 5% human sample; ~$100–300; D2).
7. Realistic noise from measured statistics. 8. **Verifier-filtered distillation** on 5–10k real-like messages with dual agreement (D2). 9. Hard negatives and contrast pairs. 10. Mixing ratios and a repetition budget (1–2 epochs over a larger unique set). 11. Auxiliary copy/lemmatize tasks. 12. Error-type-driven family weights from the wild suite (never reading wild messages).

Not recommended now: training on Haiku/Sonnet outputs without dual agreement or execution checks; more parameters before the data changes; machine re-translation of templates into Romanian.

author: Fable review
title: Experiment sequence E0–E8 (about 11 SmolLM2-135M runs over 1–2 weeks)
body:
Source: the independent Fable review, `eval/reports/current/data-improvement-plan-fable.md` (status PROPOSAL, 2026-09-29; produced read-only on the CPU from existing corpora, suites and prediction files). The plan recommends; the owner decides. Section 4. Each experiment changes one thing against the previous adopted state, with a fixed row count (~24k train); every run needs the owner's approval.

| Id | Change | Decision rule (abridged) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| E0 (CPU only) | frame-disjoint dev, novelty report, two fidelity metrics | adopt the new dev if within 5 points of test short |
| E0b | seed 43 on the baseline data | sets the noise floor |
| E1 | open names (idea 1) | adopt if the unseen-name gap at least halves, CI excluding 0 |
| E2 | open relations (2a, then 2b) | adopt if OOD EN gains ≥8 and test short does not drop |
| E3 | Romanian A/B (dictionary vs lemma targets) | recommend the higher OOD RO branch; owner decides D1 |
| E4 | length and register (ideas 4 and 7) | adopt if wild proposition F1 +0.05 |
| E5 | contrast pairs + mixing budget | adopt if yes/no or "when" +5 |
| E6 | verified paraphrase layer (after D2) | adopt if the unseen-frame gap shrinks ≥5 with 0 no-copy hits |
| E7 | distillation set (after D2) | adopt if wild accepted +4 and test short −1 at most |
| E8 | confirmation on Gemma 3 270M and SmolLM2-360M | reports feed DS010 |

Budget: about 11 GPU runs ≈ 28 h GPU (≈2.5 h each) plus ≈1.5 h CPU evaluation each. If E1–E3 already reach the §3 thresholds, E6–E7 become optional.

author: Fable review
title: Owner decisions requested: D1–D6 in questions.md (D7, D8 in the plan only)
body:
Source: the independent Fable review, `eval/reports/current/data-improvement-plan-fable.md` (status PROPOSAL, 2026-09-29; produced read-only on the CPU from existing corpora, suites and prediction files). The plan recommends; the owner decides. Section 5 and `questions.md`. Recommendations are the reviewer's.

- **D1 Romanian → English in the small model?** Options: A keep English and ship a large RO→EN dictionary through the data; B Romanian dictionary-form relations and common nouns, linked by the host through Romanian lexicon aliases; C an A/B experiment and decide on numbers. Recommendation: **C** (prior favours B for relations and common nouns).
- **D2 LLM-written data in training?** A yes with execution verification, per-row provenance, ≤~40% of the data and a 400-row review; B paraphrases only; C no. Recommendation: **A** (~$100–300 of API).
- **D3 Freeze the current sealed suites** (v1 test, OOD v1, wild) for the whole program; new data only in formalizer-v2. Recommendation: **yes**.
- **D4 Long messages capped** (≤8 statements, ≤1,200 characters) plus a 20–120-word medium family. Recommendation: **yes**.
- **D5 Approval of the experiment series** (E0–E8, ~11 runs). A approve the whole series with the plan's decision rules; B approve each experiment. questions.md recommends **A** ("I report after each experiment and you can stop the series at any time"); the plan's own §5 recommends approval per experiment id. The two texts differ; which one the owner reads as the recommendation is not recorded.
- **D6 Wild suite v2:** align the wild targets with DS021 now (202 "I/my" instead of "the user", fragments marked `no_request`, invented constraint bounds) as a new version, and commission wild-v2 with new writers after the generator changes. Recommendation: **yes**.
- D7 (plan only): per-row predicate declarations for open-vocabulary verification worlds in the pilot. D8 (plan only): a host post-check or constrained decoding for proper names, evaluated after E1.

Status at seeding (2026-09-29 08:10Z): every **Răspuns** line in questions.md is empty; no decision recorded.

author: Fable review
title: Risks the plan carries
body: Source: the independent Fable review, `eval/reports/current/data-improvement-plan-fable.md` (status PROPOSAL, 2026-09-29; produced read-only on the CPU from existing corpora, suites and prediction files). The plan recommends; the owner decides. Section 5, "Risks to carry": (1) verifier ceiling: paraphrases and distilled labels are only as right as the checks, so keep the 400-row human review and never let LLM-touched rows exceed ~40% of a build; (2) attribution: one change per run; (3) single seed: bounded by E0b; (4) a Romanian policy switch reverses a fresh owner decision (Q-DATA-6) and touches DS021, the wire docs and the host lexicon; (5) CPU evaluation time (long rows cost 29 s each): evaluate long rows only in E4 and E7; (6) GPU sharing: one worker, no concurrent jobs.

author: Fable review
title: Clause decomposition proposal: how it relates to the E0–E8 plan
body: The clause-decomposition proposal (`eval/reports/current/sop-clause-decomposition-proposal.md`) is a language change, not a data-volume change: it adds `clause TYPE $id` lines and `$id` role values so that each clause of a compound sentence is its own short wire. It is orthogonal to E1–E5 (open vocabularies, Romanian policy, length and register) and should be validated by a paired experiment, `eval-clause-decomposition-v1` (two SmolLM2-135M runs on the same 3.3k new compound rows, printed flat vs chained), sequenced after E0/E0b so seed variance is known. Migration: train/dev regenerated as formalizer-v2; sealed v1 suites stay frozen (D3) and are scored by execution equivalence; wild multi-clause rows get decomposed accepted targets in a companion file. Owner decisions L1–L6 in questions.md.

author: llm-diversify-agent
title: Idea 6 (verified paraphrase layer) is implemented; idea 8 has interfaces
body: Idea 6 of the plan is built and piloted (`eval/reports/current/llm-diversify/pilot-summary.md`): acceptance 30.6% after all filters, per-filter pass rates anchors 79.5%, cues 67.9%, execution 100%, source no-copy 100%, sealed no-copy 93.9%, judge 60.2%. The plan's section 3 leakage rules are enforced mechanically (no 8-gram or exact duplicate with any sealed suite, no distinctive 4-gram with OOD or wild, no OOD or wild name added, no sealed row or persona in any prompt), provenance is on every row, and `applyQuota` keeps LLM rows at most 40% of a build. Recommendation for E6: generate about 3 paraphrases per row over the eligible families, excluding `constraint` until it has a numeric-structure check, and run the 400-row human review before qualification. Idea 8 (distillation) waits for the new target format (D1, L1-L6): `distill.mjs` defines the pluggable format interface and refuses to run without one.

author: simplifier-agent
title: Dedicated simplifier: training-data plan (messy message → oracle simple text), awaiting Q-SIMPL-1
body: Pairs: generator train/dev rows → renderSimpleText(surface_ir) (23,817 and 5,131 rows render without error; mean 172 → 147 characters). Input side: noisy rows (7,393 train), code-switching (3,616), long messages (1,420), extra noise re-draws of the same IR, and Haiku paraphrases that inherit the IR unchanged (pilot acceptance about 34%); about 60k pairs. Sealed suites stay evaluation-only. Candidates: mT5-small (300M; whole message up to 512 tokens; about 30–60 min on GB10) and byT5-small (300M, byte-level, robust to typos and diacritics; long messages split symbolically first; about 2–3 h). Evaluation: dev 100/300/full through the UD converter with paired bootstrap and early stopping; also answer/refusal rate, name fidelity and value fold-equality. No existing model fits (survey: eval/reports/current/simplifier/models/). Recommendation: first make the converter read the oracle conventions (the oracle bound is about 1/3 today), then a paired mT5-small vs byT5-small experiment. Not trained; approval question Q-SIMPL-1.
